newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's key CUB profit rises 11.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Foster's key CUB profit rises 11.5 pct.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group Ltd said its Australian beer unit Carlton and United Breweries (CUB) increased earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) by 11.5 percent to A$187.4 million in the six months ended December 31.
Foster's said CUB's performance was the main factor behind the rise in total profitability in the 1996/97 first half.
Total EBIT rose 20.1 percent to A$231.9 million and net profit rose 2.4 percent to A$169.4 million.
"CUB had a four percent increase in the volume of beer sold, a remarkable result in a beer market which rose only 0.6 percent," Foster's chief executive Ted Kunkel said.
CUB's volume was higher in the six states and the Northern Territory, allowing the division to increase its national market share to 55 percent from 53 percent a year ago.
Analysts have recently said the division had easily increased its market battle with key rival Lion Nathan Ltd which has faced management, marketing and promotion difficulties in the last year.
Foster's said the market gains continued to be based on CUB's core brands of VB, Foster's Light Ice, Carlton Cold and Crown Lager. Sales by this group rose 14 percent.

"CUB further consolidated its position as the major beer supplier in New South Wales and, against aggressive competition, slightly increased its share in Queensland. Market share rose in each of the states," Foster's said.
The Australian operations of Lion Nathan are heavily weighted to the New South Wales and Queensland markets.
